claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with strong hysteresis under low applied fields.
The first-order transition produces a large magnetic entropy change.
Local chemical and structural heterogeneities concentrate exchange-interaction strengths in the as-deposited alloy.
A controlled subcritical anneal reduces local chemical heterogeneity.
A controlled subcritical anneal reduces local strain without changing the overall phase.
Nanoscale chemical ordering and the distribution of exchange interactions govern transition sharpness and hysteresis.
Changes in lattice parameters can modify magnetic exchange interactions.
Reducing chemical fluctuations and strain-induced exchange-energy variation broadens the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Partial homogenization lowers the nucleation or energy barriers for the phase change.
Lower phase-change barriers reduce magnetocaloric-cycle hysteresis while retaining a significant overall entropy change.
Relative to the as-deposited material, annealed samples will exhibit a broader magnetic-entropy-change peak versus temperature.
Relative to the as-deposited material, annealed samples will exhibit a smaller hysteresis width during low-field magnetization-demagnetization cycles.
Annealing may modestly reduce the peak magnetic entropy-change magnitude while improving reversible performance.
The annealed samples will provide faster heat exchange than the as-deposited samples.
The predictions apply only when annealing produces partial homogenization without complete phase transformation or degradation of magnetic ordering.
The predicted broadening and hysteresis reduction may not occur at magnetic fields significantly above the low-field regime.
The optimum annealing temperature-time profile and the quantitative trade-off between hysteresis reduction and peak entropy change are unknown.
